record.paper_title: Ten Open Problems in Connexive Logic
record.original_question: Identify the precise background assumptions needed to obtain a connexive logic as an expansion of FDE that is introduced semantically by means of the Australian plan.

evidence.quote: Open problem 7 What are the precise background assumptions that are required to obtain a connexive logic as an expansion of FDE, introduced semantically in terms of the Australian plan?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. The logic FDE (first-degree entailment) is the four-valued paraconsistent and paracomplete logic in the language with conjunction, disjunction, and a De Morgan negation, whose semantics assigns each formula a subset of {T, F} (the values "told true", "told false"), with standard relational support-of-truth and support-of-falsity clauses for the binary connectives and the clause that ¬A is supported as true (resp. false) iff A is supported as false (resp. true).

A connexive logic is a logic that validates the following theses (and whose conditional is non-symmetric):
 (Aristotle) ¬(¬A → A) and ¬(A → ¬A);
 (Boethius)  (A → B) → ¬(A → ¬B) and (A → ¬B) → ¬(A → B).

The "Australian plan" approach to negation and conditionals in non-classical logics employs a Routley–Meyer ternary relational frame ⟨W, R, *⟩ in which negation is interpreted by means of the Routley star *: W → W via
 w ⊩ ¬A  iff  w* ⊮ A,
and implication is interpreted by means of the ternary accessibility relation R via
 w ⊩ A → B  iff  ∀x, y (Rwxy and x ⊩ A ⟹ y ⊩ B).

Problem. Determine the precise frame conditions (i.e., the conditions on the ternary relation R, on the Routley star *, on the set of designated/normal worlds, and on the relationship between R and *) that are necessary and sufficient in order that an extension of FDE obtained by adding an Australian-plan implication be a connexive logic, in the sense of validating the Aristotle and Boethius theses (and falsifying their converses where required for non-symmetry).
artifact.status_search_result: General surveys (e.g., the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy entry on connexive logic) discuss both American-plan and Australian-plan approaches to connexive expansions of FDE, but no source located identifies a definitive set of frame conditions characterizing exactly when an Australian-plan expansion of FDE yields a connexive logic. The status appears unresolved in the literature accessible by web search.

status_evidence.title: Connexive Logic (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
status_evidence.snippet: connexive logic was subjected to semantical investigations based on ternary frames for relevance logics, making use of the Routley star negation that is distinctive of logics on the Australian Plan
status_evidence.claim: The Australian-plan semantics for connexive logics uses Routley–Meyer ternary frames with the Routley star, but precise general background conditions for connexivity are not pinned down.
